questions.question: Historically, how did people once describe the shape of the Earth and the movement of the stars and Sun?
options: The Earth was flat, and all the stars and the Sun moved around it.
The Earth was a sphere, and it moved around a flat Sun.
The Earth was flat, but it spun while the stars remained completely still.
The Earth was a sphere, and it remained still at the absolute edge of the universe.

questions.question: Up until which century did the majority of people believe that the Earth was located at the very centre of the universe?
options: The 12th century
The 16th century
The 19th century
The 21st century

questions.question: Which scientific instrument has provided critical observational evidence to help us develop our understanding of the universe?
options: Microscope
Barometer
Telescope
Seismometer

questions.question: What is the angle of the tilt of the axis on which the Earth spins?
options: 12.5 degrees
23.5 degrees
45.0 degrees
90.0 degrees

questions.question: In what direction does gravity pull objects when they are near massive bodies like planets, moons, or stars?
options: Towards the center of the massive body
Away from the surface into outer space
In a sideways direction parallel to the equator
Towards the magnetic north pole only

questions.question: How does the mass of an object affect the strength of its gravitational pull?
options: The greater the mass, the weaker its gravity.
The greater the mass, the stronger its gravity.
The mass of an object has no effect on its gravity.
Gravity only depends on the size, not the mass of the object.

questions.question: What is the effect of Earth's gravity pulling the Moon towards the centre of the Earth?
options: It causes the Moon to spin faster on its own axis.
It pushes the Moon further away into deep space.
It changes the Moon's direction, keeping it in orbit around Earth.
It stops the Moon from rotating at all.

questions.question: Why does the Earth continuously change its direction and orbit around the Sun?
options: Because the Sun's gravity pulls Earth towards the centre of the Sun.
Because magnetic fields repel the Earth away from the outer solar system.
Because solar winds push the Earth in a circular path.
Because the Earth's oceans create a tidal drag that pulls it around.

questions.question: What happens to rays of light when they hit a surface face-on compared to when they hit at an angle?
options: They are more spread out when they hit face-on.
They are less spread out when they hit face-on.
They change color when they hit at an angle.
They reflect completely and do not heat the surface at all.

questions.question: At what time of day is the heating effect of the Sun greatest at any given place on Earth?
options: At sunrise
At midday
At sunset
At midnight

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a planet?
options: A small piece of ice that burns up in the atmosphere.
An extremely large sphere of hot gas that gives out its own light.
A very large sphere of rock or gas that orbits a star.
A cluster of billions of stars grouped together in space.

questions.question: What does our solar system consist of?
options: Only the Earth and the Moon.
The Sun and all the objects that orbit the Sun.
Every star and planet in our galaxy.
A collection of distant galaxies that do not contain stars.

questions.question: How do the distances between objects in our solar system compare to the actual sizes of those objects?
options: The distances are very, very large compared to the sizes of the objects.
The distances are roughly equal to the diameters of the objects.
The objects are so close together that they constantly touch.
The distances are extremely small compared to the sizes of the objects.

questions.question: What are the seasons in the Northern and Southern hemispheres in December?
options: Both hemispheres experience summer.
Both hemispheres experience winter.
The Northern hemisphere has summer, and the Southern hemisphere has winter.
The Northern hemisphere has winter, and the Southern hemisphere has summer.

questions.question: Why do countries near the Equator not experience distinct summer and winter seasons?
options: They are tilted completely away from the Sun all year.
They stay close to 'face-on' to the Sun all year.
They do not receive any light rays from the Sun.
They are shielded by the Earth's thickest clouds all year.

questions.question: Why do the stars in the night sky appear much smaller and dimmer than our Sun?
options: Because they are much further away.
Because they do not emit any light of their own.
Because they are covered by cosmic dust clouds.
Because they are physically smaller than a standard planet.

questions.question: What is a light-year?
options: The time it takes for Earth to orbit the Sun once.
The distance that light travels in one year.
The time it takes for light to travel from the Sun to the Earth.
The distance from the Earth to the nearest star.

questions.question: What are galaxies in the universe?
options: Solid rings of dust orbiting a single planet.
Groups of stars, with billions of stars in each group.
Small groups of up to ten planets orbiting a moon.
Clouds of gas containing only a single star.

questions.question: Which motion of the Earth explains the cycle of day and night?
options: Earth's orbit around the Sun.
Earth's spin.
Earth's tilt changing back and forth.
Earth's orbit around the Moon.

questions.question: Which shape best describes the path of Earth's orbit around the Sun?
options: A highly elongated oval
A perfect square
An almost perfect circle
A random spiral
